title: Count and index shortest binary chart words (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped algebraic proof with finite corroboration: two binary Lagrangian charts in dimension 2n, at distance r, have exactly the following minimum-length words.

```text
minimum length        r
chart paths           P(r) = product_(j=1)^r (2^j-1)
literal axis words    W(n,r) = 2^(r(n-1)) P(r)
```

An exact lexicographic rank/unrank bijection indexes every shortest literal word. A uniform integer index therefore gives a uniform word. The written proof covers all n>=1; the bounded reference implementation accepts 1<=n<=6. This adds shortest-word counting/indexing to Dugongue's #4841 single/paired-neighborhood work; no predecessor executable is replayed. The underlying finite symplectic geometry is classical, with no literature-priority claim. No new kappa is claimed.

This contribution is produced by Nick Petalas. Credit Dugongue #4841, Cinna Davis #4690, Cao Yifan #4610, Yiyang #4710, the retained native caller #4713/#4630/#4635, and their predecessor notices. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

## Evidence

- Before: the cited single/paired-neighborhood result supplies one-step chart moves, without this package's shortest-word count and indexing contract.
- After: independent intersection-graph BFS covers every ordered pair of all 3, 15 and 135 charts at n=1,2,3, totaling 18,459 pairs. The literal checker exhausts 28,386 minimum-length axis tuples through n=2, including 1,644 successful words, and checks every successful word's exact rank/unrank. There are 58 larger round trips through n=6 and eleven rejection controls.
- Warning-strict normal and optimized registered checks pass locally on CPython 3.12.15, macOS arm64, in 5.39s and 5.41s. Both produce identical generated receipts bound to all six package files. Package metadata/replay and exact committed-byte/source-history preflight pass. Committed export integrity and a Git-free replay pass. An independent read-only proof/code review found no correctness gap.

From the repository root:

```sh

/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/shortest-chart-axis-words/verify.py

/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/shortest-chart-axis-words --check-source-history
```

Expected status: `PASS_SHORTEST_CHART_AXIS_WORDS`. A clean Python 3.12 interpreter can replace the exact local path. Standard library only. Source provenance is canonical main `624de9dc66858af0945e5f8a0942488d62280d43`, revision 7; submission fetch found no guidance/source change. The cached card scan covers 379 open PRs and 3,855 Discussion records; 6,194 tracked local note paths were outside its sparse coverage. Live open PRs, recent claims, merged-term searches and distinctive all-main README searches were checked again before committing. Search coverage is not a novelty certificate.

The historical card control raises `KeyError: 'complex_profile'` against the selected schema. The current `research_selected_baseline.py` source-binding control passes. This orientation failure does not enter the new theorem or verifier.

## Limitations

The count concerns syntactically distinct nonzero-axis sequences and chart paths. Distinct full symplectic products and physical phase lifts can have different equivalence classes. This is not a native supplier, a complete multiplication theorem or a selected-frontier update. Paid profile, other incident edges, dirty restoration, ownership, precision, compiler and outer admission remain unrun. The code provides an exact indexing contract rather than a random-number generator. No Lean, Docker, historical suite or selected cold replay was run.

## Open next questions

- Avoid scanning every ambient axis by constructing pairing-one quotient axes directly. Start with a canonical basis and an explicitly declared ordering; practical nine-bit indexing remains unimplemented.
- Classify distinct full symplectic products of shortest chart words. Start by enumerating product matrices for transverse n=2 endpoints; product/phase equivalence is outside the delivered contract.

## Related open work

- #4841 supplies complete single/paired chart neighborhoods and the corrected one-step tariff; this contribution counts and indexes shortest paths/words between two endpoints.
- The separate cycle-constrained multi-chart-neighborhood [claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19133726) studies simultaneous transported block moves, rather than minimum-length endpoint words. No competing numerical quantity is compared.
